text:
mara: quick heads-up — ran a focused perf pass on the canary (10.2.4) after the recent kernel selector tweak. seeing a host-side CPU regression for small requests (<16 tokens). flamegraph + perf data uploaded: https://s3.redwood/internal/ingress/1747777000/fg.html

shane: can you paste the top hotspots? small requests are our biggest tail for hosted customers right now.

mara: sure, paste of perf top (sorted by samples):
```
  samples  command  symbol
  4200    runtime   token::tokenize_utf8
  1800    runtime   grpc::writev_loop
  1100    runtime   request::parse_headers
   800    runtime   memcpy
   200    runtime   kernel_selector::choose
```
exported collapsed stacks -> flamegraph at the link. overall host CPU up ~28% vs previous build under same traffic mix (p95 small requests).

anya: interesting that kernel_selector shows low samples but we're still slower. my hunch: selector picks the multi-kernel path for short seqs because of the new heuristics, but the multi-kernel path has per-call overhead that dominates at short seqs. in other words: wrong kernel choice for low-token, low-latency requests.

ops-lee: confirmed on my repro: forcing the legacy single-kernel for seq<=32 drops CPU by ~18% on that traffic slice. can we gate selector to prefer single-kernel for seq<32 while we dig in?

mara: i'm +1 for a temporary gate. propose config change and small canary:
```
runtime:
  kernel_selector:
    prefer_single_for_short_seq: true
    short_seq_threshold: 32
```
we should also add an observability metric: kernel_choice_histogram by seq_len and latency bucket.

shane: also seeing grpc::writev_loop as second hotspot — that's the ingress framing layer. are we coalescing small frames aggressively enough? maybe small writes per token are killing us when tokenization emits many fragments.

anya: yes — two-pronged fix: (1) kernel-selection gate, (2) increase coalesce window for short requests (coalesce_ms from 2 -> 8) for the canary. try both independently.

runtime-bot: [alert] perf_regression.host_cpu_increase detected at 2026-03-22T12:17:15Z (metric > 20% over baseline for 5m). Ticket auto-filed: PERF-17477.

ops-lee: I'll spin two canaries: A) kernel gate only, B) coalesce window only, C) both. tagging shard a/b/c and collecting tokenization traces + writev histograms. expected run 30m each.

mara: for traces, run this lightweight capture on the host:
```
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30 && perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold
# upload out.fold
```
also capture tcpdump of ingress small writes: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w smallwrites.pcap port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-push) != 0`

shane: i'll add an experiment in the router to pass a header X-Kernel-Hint to force single-kernel so we don't need a code change for quick rollout. good to have the config change too for longer-term.

anya: long-term action items: add unit perf tests for sequences 1..64, add kernel path microbench in CI, and add an integration that measures tokenization fragmentation per request. capturing that now will help avoid regressions.

mara: sounds good. ops-lee, can you post the canary IDs + results here in ~1h? if A or C looks good we'll flip the gate on canary in prod and push an A/B to 10% first. :thumbsup:

ops-lee: will do — kicking off now.

mara: thanks — will follow up with the flamegraphs and kchoice histograms once runs complete.
